# #486 written plan — revision 03 · 1/5 · README.md

# #486 · Authored failures at execution boundaries

Revision 03 is the GPT architecture proposal for a targeted independent Claude Fable 5.2 xhigh recheck. The source is signed main `02351e2fb932b3be44e7cc3fb3943a61d568226c`, tree `d289bb12b943557584c5659bc33447d1baebc2f6`. The coordinator recommends fixed field and cause text for every newly projected JSONata runtime rejection, including a direct literal `$error`. It identifies the failing field and gives a correction without publishing the argument. The evaluator may supply a more specific fixed reason only from a source-owned branch of the same invocation. The private 40-case planning probe supports this amendment. Fable 01 returned **REVISE PLAN** on revision 01. Attempt 02 reached quota before a verdict. Attempt 03 must assess this packet after the 11:00 UTC reset. A real verdict and separately catalogued delegated selection precede implementation. The issue retains `needs-plan-approval`. Owner review of delegated decisions and any rework precede owner QA. [Issue](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/486) · [admission](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/279#issuecomment-7059835778) · [D171](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/427#issuecomment-7059806202)

[Provenance decision and exact alternatives](expression-provenance.md) · [26 boundary decisions](boundaries.md) · [negative controls, acceptance and affected files](verification.md) · [critique dispositions](critique-disposition.md) · [source bindings](manifest.json)

## Source-owned public causes

1. Reuse `TEMPLATE_ERROR`, `EXPRESSION_ERROR` and `MUTATION_ERROR`. Newly recognized authored errors are non-resumable because the run pins its definition and re-execution can repeat work. Refer the author to the field and a corrected version. Existing explicit Replay remains a separate run with ordinary observation and consent requirements. Preserve abort, stop, deadline and termination handling.
2. Call a concrete evaluator on prepared arguments at each authorized site. Render through the concrete renderer, report selector location and item index at the predicate, and prepare views and JSON conversions outside. For JSONata use the invocation-scoped evaluation outcome described in the provenance decision. A failure during preparation or predicate coercion takes the existing site fallback. An error supplied by an external caller preserves its existing handling and carries no author-origin proof. The inference transform mapper shares narrow operation hooks with Mutate while supplying its own safe public copy. An arbitrary port rejection has its established handling even if its class is a real domain error.
3. The public message includes a fixed field label and safe reason plus one-based ordinal when relevant. JSON details use fixed `boundary`, zero-based indices, finite `operationKind` where applicable and `cause:{code,message}`. For maps and headers, ordinal means the order of `Object.entries` on the pinned object: own enumerable string keys, array-index keys first in ascending order, other string keys in insertion order. Do not publish headers, user-chosen map names, file paths, templates, echoed values, schema data or exception details as locators. Receipt/beat count or completed file count may be reported only when observed. **Reserve top-level `details.childRunId`, `childNodeId`, and `childDetails` exclusively for the existing actual child-failure wrapper.**
4. Construct each new public cause from a fixed vocabulary. For Liquid use its parse/render reason and validated numeric token location when reliably available. For JSONata use a fixed compile, unsafe-regex, depth or time direction only when GraphGoblin observes the corresponding local failure branch. An ordinary runtime rejection at an eligible data-only field gets a location-specific direction such as “The selector could not evaluate this item. Check its input type.” This describes the failed operation. Every new projection omits JSONata arguments, source, raw numeric/library error codes, raw runtime positions, asserted messages and literal labels. Decision route expressions keep their existing fixed copy. Retain the safe fixed directions for target, patch, regex and schema operations. Keep facts invocation-local, outside `DomainError.details`. Cap the composed cause at 1,000 UTF-16 units including ellipsis and apply the existing 10,000-unit failure-message ceiling.
5. Existing logging and public contracts still apply at their original sites. The new JSONata observation records only fixed phase/reason values. It does not collect raw exception text, stack, details or expression source for diagnostics. A legacy error reference can transit the existing rejection path when identity or behavior requires it. For other new authored/canonical internal diagnostics, the existing private correlation design permits one run/node/field log record with turn ID when known. General harness, historical rows, P01/P02 and B25 retain their established text contracts. Unknown harness errors can already publish adapter-supplied text, and the file-return channel can publish a bounded external error message. Use separate synthetic markers for these controls.

## Inference, in execution order

- Reconstruct the logical visit from events. Guard `delivery-uncertain && !canContinueTurn(pending)` **before** model resolution; that guard needs no model and retains the existing recovery failure. Otherwise resolve model/effort. `session-missing` then uses those resolved facts to form the existing actionable missing-session failure, before workspace/transforms/files. If the resolver itself fails, attach known prior turn provenance as **information only** to the existing typed/error projection. Preserve its code, text, details and resumability (restorable catalogue failure remains resumable). Do not manufacture model/effort or emit a missing-session failure without the required facts. A later eligible Resume can restore resolution and reach the original fresh-session action. [`inference.ts:295–367`, `run-manager.ts:1540–1559,2444–2492`, `inference-turn.ts:159–182`]
- Separate pre-intent preparation from invocation. For a known prior pending task attach its original `provenance(pending)` (IDs, kind, actual submission and session) to preparation failures without creating a new intent, submission/status write, acceptance marker or cleanup of an old handle. New visits omit that field. The existing earlier `run.failed.inference.retry` reconstructs the exact otherwise-unrecorded prompt, harness, optional context and selected session. A later failure without `retry` updates the existing pending task. Preserve the fold; no new retry object or `intentUnconfirmed` flag is emitted for preparation. Respect bypass on saved prompt, exact positive refusal retry, usable-session continuation, and explicit fresh-session selection both with and without a saved prompt. Eligible attempts still reconstruct transformed views and materialize files as today, including the context used by repair. Earlier successful coerce calls/file writes can survive a later authored failure; add no retry or compensating writes. Exactly-once prep across a crash before recorded intent is outside this contract. [`inference.ts:303–396,445–532`, `inference-turn.ts:36–80,109–136`]
- B17's two rare rerenders operate on recognized *system* prompt constants after the first render succeeded. Locally map the pure rerender rejection to the existing safe engine-owned `INTERNAL_ERROR` projection, current inference node, ordinary internal pre-turn resumability (true). Keep cloning, view construction and `window.fits` outside both concrete renderer catches. Retain the surrounding timeout-disposal/abort priority and existing `contextWindow`/`fits` provider mapping. A direct typed internal projection can pass the existing typed-error branch; no general harness mapper change is needed. Saved/fresh prompts remain ineligible for trimming. [`inference-context.ts:13–17,42–70`, `inference.ts:397–443`]
- At B18/B19 only, tag the **source-owned** failure when repair prompt rendering or output mutation fails after a successful provider result. Keep the last actual turn ID, kind, session and visit; B18 precedes establishing the next repair intent. If this mapped cause survives normal cleanup/timeout/evidence precedence, add fixed `details.phase:"after-result"` and a sentence such as **“GraphGoblin received the provider result before this step failed.”** Keep conservative `delivery-uncertain` for its unfinished graph persistence (a result cannot mean an unsent turn); store through the existing submission path. Never synthesize an acceptance marker or alter the durable-acceptance rules. The winner is non-resumable even with a usable session. For exactly that winning after-result cause omit the generic unusable-session uncertainty suffix, even if the harness reported no session. If a higher-ranked pinned refusal, missing-session, termination, cancellation, stop or timeout wins, it keeps its existing code, copy, metadata and recovery. Use source-specific ownership of the winning failure, never merely a `details.phase` key test on arbitrary port errors. Artifact publication, invalid provider output and post-result storage failures keep their current publication and submission policies. [`inference.ts:598–705,707–879`, `inference-turn.ts:136–182`]
- The harness evidence fold, adapters, provider text, retry, submission fallback and family-specific resumability stay intact. Verify actual same-class exceptions **and** name/code lookalikes at every callback against the explicit table. Synchronous throw before a handle, iterator/result rejection after a handle, prior stronger evidence and secondary cleanup are different observations. Preserve #427's recognized pinned refusal text and existing suppression of an automatic resend after acceptance. [`inference.ts:198–267,537–590,709–712,797–874`, `inference-failure.ts:52–98,104–167`]

## Workspace, child ownership and persistence

On a successful directory cache miss, RunManager passes `WorkspacePort.resolve(resolvedSpec,runId)` the existing temp or fixed spec union members only. For a template, on the engine side precompute the view, render directly, apply the identical `.trim()`, and convert a nonempty result to fixed. A genuine template rejection or empty trimmed result returns a local invalid-template value. Keep fixed paths as given, existing relative→absolute/mkdir behavior, temp ownership and fixed/shared canonical-use journal. No second public spec, stored schema, migration, format or history rewrite. Set the directory cache only after successful port resolution. Node callers convert the invalid-template value to the node's typed error. A thrown port exception stays outside that conversion. [`run-manager.ts:2506,3338–3351`, `infrastructure/src/fs/{workspace.ts:14–35,owned-resources.ts:92–124}`]

In the existing file-channel try block, an engine-local invalid-template result supplies the safe bounded delivery message and skips port resolve/write. Feed this one path into the **existing** failure-receipt catch (e.g. throw an ordinary error constructed solely from the local safe message). Keep the success receipt append inside the existing channel try, its existing catch with `describeError(error).slice(0,4000)` and the failed-receipt append where they are. Other channel inputs, logging/error text, receipt persistence/reconciliation and terminal run status retain their behavior. This adds no public run failure, duplicate receipt attempt or new delivery retry mechanism. [`run-manager.ts:2961–3038`, `adversarial.test.ts:379–417`]

Parent input evaluation precedes atomic child admission. Parent output mapping runs after the child's actual terminal result; retain bundled `child_run.finished` records with its own success/failure and deduplication by terminal sequence. Parent mapping faults use the parent subloop node, bounded location/cause and no child-failure keys. For actual failed children use the existing wrapper, unchanged. Follow its linked child snapshot for authoritative `failure.inference` including retry evidence, and follow the next link at depth two. No projection copies the child's turn into the parent. Existing `childFailureForPublication` and legacy sanitization/ownership stay intact. [`subloop.ts:188–231,238–326`, `failure-publication.ts:48–56,88–130`, `run-recovery.ts:61–83`]

Stored failure JSON and `run.failed` share one new projection, with current message bounds. REST snapshots and MCP full results can carry structured details; their reduced summaries and the inspector alert need useful standalone messages. The optional typed phase and bounded cause fit current JSON details. This scoped design avoids global error dispatch, replay of deterministic failures, a durable transformed-thread snapshot, changes to historical records, and changes to public/provider policy elsewhere. Independent QA, opposite-family review, exact-head/current-target CI, coverage and the reserved final audit remain separate gates.

# #486 written plan — revision 03 · 3/5 · expression-provenance.md

# JSONata provenance decision requested from the coordinator

## Recommendation

Use a fixed cause naming the affected authored field and a corrective action on every newly recognized runtime expression failure. For example, a failed custom output expression can say “The subloop output patch expression could not be evaluated. Check the mapping against the child result.” A failed selector can name the collection and item ordinal. A transform can name its operation index and kind. Preserve the proposed cause code, failure owner, recovery policy and actual observed effects from the boundary matrix. A direct literal `$error` on ordinary stored run data qualifies for the same field-level diagnostic. Its literal stays private. B20 continues to use its existing decision-route message. This choice gives up the author-supplied short reason in the new copy.

Ask Fable to assess this choice and the two separate grounds for recording a fact below. Root must catalogue its own selection after the provider verdict. Revision 02's signed-source bindings, the original critique and the independent probe are retained as input. [Revision 02](../i4-486-architecture-02/README.md) · [actual original critique](../i4-486-fable-plan-critique-01/provider/provider-final-message.md) · [40-case planning report](../i4-486-jsonata-contract-01/REPORT.md)

## What the source establishes

The package exports `evaluateExpression`, `evaluatePredicate`, `ExpressionOptions` and the domain error classes. Its evaluator accepts arbitrary JavaScript inputs and an optional record of unknown binding values. The cached parser and internal `expressionAst` are implementation details. Today the same try covers construction of the effective bindings, including the options/budget reads, and the awaited evaluator call. Its catch forwards an existing ExpressionError by identity and wraps other errors with the same message policy and expression details. Predicate truthiness runs after that promise succeeds. The API maps public DomainError.details into its existing error response. [Domain evaluator](G:/ggq/gg-i4-486-authored-errors/GraphGoblin/packages/domain/src/expression.ts) · [exports](G:/ggq/gg-i4-486-authored-errors/GraphGoblin/packages/domain/src/index.ts) · [domain errors](G:/ggq/gg-i4-486-authored-errors/GraphGoblin/packages/domain/src/errors.ts) · [API error projection](G:/ggq/gg-i4-486-authored-errors/GraphGoblin/apps/api/src/plugins/errors.ts)

The 40 predeclared probe predictions matched. S02/S03 demonstrate indistinguishable public projections for genuine and replacement calls. S06/S11 identify binding preparation as a failure site separate from evaluator invocation. S10 proves identity/details preservation. S04/S05 establish omission of inherited and non-enumerable bindings. S07 establishes that an own binding can be the real built-in. S08/S09 distinguish the actual binding name from an input field. S12 is one sequential cached-source control. The source of the inspected engine call sites supplies default bindings or freshly built plain `{thread,index}` data. No serialized-loop path to arbitrary JavaScript callback execution was established. These planner observations do not test a production classifier.

## Concrete evaluator boundary

1. Keep the existing public evaluator functions, options, error constructors, compiler cache and predicate truthiness. Use one underlying implementation. The new engine path needs only a narrow, in-memory outcome from a concrete expression or predicate invocation on its prepared inputs. A practical shape is a value on success or a rejection with the existing error reference for legacy handling and one closed phase/reason. Use a small domain entry point for this observation under the explicit public export list. Its interfaces take a source and concrete arguments. Existing callers keep their ordinary value/rejection contract. Add no caller-supplied promise/function parameter to assert provenance. No engine import of `expressionAst` or deep domain modules.
2. Observe compile failure at the actual parser call on a source string, and unsafe regex at GraphGoblin’s explicit rejection. Observe time/depth only where the **current invocation’s own** budget check actually raises the failure that reaches its boundary. The evidence may retain a local identity for that invocation if needed to establish the winning limit cause. An absorbed inner failure or an unmatched rejection gets generic fixed copy at an eligible site. The finite reasons carry no raw message, supplied error fields, name, raw code, stack, AST value, runtime position or arbitrary details. No data goes on DomainError.details, enumerable properties, the compile cache or a process-wide error registry. Returning the same error later, at another site or in an overlapping invocation, cannot transfer a prior cause.
3. Separate **binding preparation** from **the await of the concrete evaluator**. Prepare exactly once, in the present order, with the present spread and overrides. Getters can run even on unrelated enumerable keys. A preparation exception follows the same legacy wrapping or same-object pass-through as today. Give it no positive evaluation or author-origin fact. In the evaluation catch an ordinary raw rejection can establish only that this one call rejected. An existing externally supplied ExpressionError likewise retains its identity/details and provides no source-specific reason. Do not inspect or copy its class/code/message/details for a new fact. The JSONata `CHECKED_EVAL` path can forward internal ExpressionErrors too. On an eligible data-only run path a nested/dynamic failure can use the generic runtime direction. It needs no reconstruction of the inner rejection.
4. The engine may use that neutral **evaluation-rejected** observation to identify the failed field only at a newly covered, explicit authored site with an expression from the pinned definition, inert run inputs from an established data source, and the closed binding construction used at that site. Examples include a stored thread view, the JSON-converted probe result, a child result from the store, or an item from those views with the locally assembled thread/index bindings. Ownership here is the operation and field that failed. Calling an arbitrary binding on the low-level API supplies no evidence of a built-in or deterministic author error. An unknown or external input/port provenance stays on its prior error path. A JS object type assertion or same-class exception cannot establish the data origin. If an implementation site cannot identify the concrete source of its inert data, keep its existing fallback and flag that site in verification. No new scan, clone, serialization or validation of arbitrary JavaScript inputs is required.
5. For a predicate, let the same-call expression outcome carry to the predicate site. Keep evaluation-success truthiness outside the new rejection observation. `Array.isArray`, array length and `Object.keys(value).length` belong to coercion. A coercion failure propagates as before with no authored marker. For a transformation, carry the concrete expression/predicate outcome only to the existing narrow per-operation hook for the new inference mapper. The hook at `mutations.ts:89–91,119` encloses the evaluator and leaves `asJson` outside. One implementation is an optional fact argument delivered solely to the new inference mapper at that immediate rejection site. Preserve the original three-argument mapping invocation and error for existing callers, including P01. Clock, ID, structured completion, conversion and storage errors receive no evaluator fact. Never rediscover a cause in the executor catch or by inspecting saved errors. [Mutation sites](G:/ggq/gg-i4-486-authored-errors/GraphGoblin/packages/domain/src/mutations.ts) · [engine selectors and transform hooks](G:/ggq/gg-i4-486-authored-errors/GraphGoblin/packages/engine/src/handlers/common.ts)

A fixed generic reason is appropriate when the eligible authored invocation rejected but lacks a more specific source-owned reason. Failure to establish the authored site, input origin, or evaluation phase instead leaves the existing internal/external fallback in charge. Existing return receipts, adapter messages, B20, B25 and historical/P01/P02 diagnostics have their own public contracts.

## Alternative considered

The narrow alternative would preserve an optional direct-root literal only on an explicitly owned **data-only** invocation. It would require successful once-only binding preparation, absence of an own `error` property on the resulting ordinary effective binding object, exact root function/variable `error` with one string-literal argument in the pinned AST, a matching built-in-owned D3137 during evaluation, and validation of the entire decoded literal against the chosen public-copy policy. A grouped block, nested/conditional call, dynamic message/`$eval`, assertion or external source would receive fixed copy. A conservatively excluded own binding would receive fixed copy even when it is the actual built-in. Inherited or non-enumerable `error` on the supplied bindings is omitted by the existing spread. Inspecting the *prepared* object avoids a second read of a getter. A qualifying case would take its label from the AST alone.

The binding guard plus two catch scopes would address the observed own-binding replacement and preparation seams. They cannot prove that the built-in threw on the general low-level API. Even for a literal expression the pinned evaluator may inspect an array input while setting up its environment before it evaluates the AST (`jsonata.js:5650–5654,7532–7534`). That source observation was outside the 40 executed cases. Raw library error codes, class names, function-shaped flags or a captured function identity would not prove that evaluation reached that function. A narrower justification must bind the input and invocation to a known inert run-data path and verify that the accepted throw came from this path. That adds AST policy, raw-code capture and a larger test contract solely to publish one piece of authored text. Revision 03 recommends dropping the exception. It needs neither a built-in identity manager nor inspection of raw D3137.

For the alternative only, the revision 02 text permits 1–128 decoded ASCII characters from `[A-Za-z0-9 _-]`, including a space-only label. JSONata does not impose that policy. The no-flags terminal-newline control rejected its newline input on the pinned runtime. There is no observed end-anchor bypass. The recommended fixed copy requires no alphabet, length check, trimming or AST classifier. [Probe report](../i4-486-jsonata-contract-01/REPORT.md) · [pinned JSONata bytes](../i4-486-jsonata-contract-01/dependency-inputs/jsonata.js)

## Focused implementation verification

| Site | Positive and negative controls for the selected fixed-copy proposal |
| --- | --- |
| Public domain compatibility, `packages/domain/src/expression.test.ts` | Exercise through the public entry as well as the new narrow observation. Compare return values and existing rejection class, code, message and details on controlled fixtures. Assert same-object identity for a supplied ExpressionError thrown by a callback or binding getter. For enumerable getters on `error` and an unrelated name expect one getter read, legacy wrapping or exact passthrough as applicable, and no evaluation fact. Successful callback returns remain successful. Cover the two replacement forms, inherited/non-enumerable omissions, own actual built-in, literal binding-name and input-field controls from S01–S11. External ordinary callback rejection may identify the call stage internally, with zero source-specific reason and no new public fields. |
| Domain reason and invocation lifetime, same test file | On a concrete compiler syntax failure, unsafe regex, real depth or controlled deadline check assert the corresponding local fixed reason. On a runtime failure without a winning local reason assert only the neutral phase. Check the same cached source in successful, failing, sequential and overlapping evaluations with independent diagnostics. Preserve the existing cache, deadline and bindings tests. Rethrow an earlier authentic error through a *later* controlled callback and verify that identity survives and the new invocation acquires no earlier reason. No universal rejection marker or AST/cache state. |
| Domain predicates, same test file | Preserve successful true/false/null/array/object outcomes. A failed expression in a predicate reaches the same evaluation-phase classification on eligible data. A controlled failure at the post-evaluation coercion operation has no authored fact and preserves the original rejection. Use an isolated coercion seam if JSONata would touch a hostile fixture earlier. Record the stage actually exercised. Do not count a fabricated coercion failure as end-to-end reachability. |
| Engine authored fields, `packages/engine/src/handlers/{flow,heartbeat-visit,mutation-failures}.test.ts`, existing inference and child suites | Verify positive public location, cause, action, node and exact recovery at a real engine expression site, a predicate and both inference transform arms. Ordinary direct literal, grouped/nested/taken conditional, dynamic and assertion failures use the same fixed field/direction at that site. Untaken/successful forms still succeed. Check direct literal plus input-derived markers never enter the new authored failure projection, including B18/B19 phase precedence where relevant. Validate existing P01/P02 and B20 outputs independently. A port throwing a same-class, same-spelling or previously genuine evaluator error keeps its legacy handling, with no new phase. |
| API and public surfaces, `apps/api/src/{subloop-failure,prompt-failure-boundaries}.test.ts` and existing API/MCP/DOM QA | Assert parity of new fixed causes across the row, corresponding run-failure event, REST snapshot, MCP full result and the visible alert. Treat stored loop definitions and legacy public error text as separate data. Real B25 request-side rejection and adjacent surfaces keep their established status, text, details and effects. Verify no raw exception text newly logged by the observer. |

These are proposed implementation checks. The retained planning validation exercised the current low-level API and pinned dependency. It did not execute a new domain observer, engine/API feature, provider path, or browser acceptance case.

## Per-site external controls

Use isolated public-method fixtures with one fault at a time and no unrelated timeout/abort unless specified. For each evaluator-adjacent external call compare (a) a true domain `TemplateError` or `ExpressionError`, (b) a plain Error with the same name, (c) a plain object with the same code and message. A retained earlier higher-ranked observation wins; positive/observed acceptance prevents a later D downgrade. [`inference-failure.ts:39–98,104–167`, `inference-turn.ts:136–182`, `inference.ts:707–879`]

| Source and controlled condition | Public code, submission and eligibility to assert |
| --- | --- |
| `contextWindow` or `window.fits` throws ordinary domain-shaped error, before new intent | `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED`, generic harness message + adapterCode; H, no new submission. On re-entry only prior informational provenance if known. Recognized context limit/unsupported retains its specific code/false. A real node timeout before admission is `INFERENCE_TIMEOUT`/true, abort follows existing priority. A failure solely in the canonical rerender is the contrasting engine-owned B17 case. |

The same later D after positive acceptance stays Q and follows the existing uncertainty conversion. |
| Harness error event plus later wrapper/cleanup | Keep existing rank and later-on-tie fold. 3. **Native effects and recovery.** Use real filesystem directories/context files, real disk-backed SQLite, a native child script appending to a disposable counter file, and a real loopback HTTP listener counting requests through the production probe adapter. # ACCEPT REVISED PLAN — revision 03

Revision 03's two amendments resolve the provenance ambiguities the 40-case probe found, and I found no regression against behaviour pinned at `02351e2`. R1–R6 remain resolved. Two one-sentence clarifications (A1, A2 below) should be folded in at selection; neither needs another recheck. This is planning only: I ran nothing and edited nothing, and the original REVISE PLAN verdict on revision 01 stands as history.

## S4, the phase observer: sound

- **The three phases exist in source.** One `try` covers the binding spread, the budget reads and the awaited call (`packages/domain/src/expression.ts:143–155`). Predicate coercion runs afterwards (`:204–208`). Splitting them with identical catch bodies changes no value or rejection.
- **Compile and unsafe-regex facts are already per call.** Both throw before `cache.set` (`:58–75`), so a failing source is re-parsed every time and nothing needs caching.
- **Depth and time need no marker on the error.**
  - The hooks are a per-call closure (`:166–187`).
  - Pinned JSONata rethrows the same object (`jsonata.js:4935–4944, 5029–5036, 5696–5699`).
  - `$eval` unwraps to the inner error by identity (`expression.ts:122–135`).
  - So a closure-local record of what this call's hook threw is enough, and it cannot transfer to another call.
- **The data-only precondition holds at every listed site by construction**, so it is a static property and needs no runtime scan.
  - B05: `heartbeat.ts:137–138`, with the probe already `toJson` output (`:42,84,98`).
  - B07/B13/B22: `common.ts:121,136`, bindings literally `{thread, index}`.
  - B08, B10, B11, B12: `subloop.ts:61, 222, 99–105, 139`, default bindings.
  - B14/B19: `mutations.ts:91,119`.
  - Threads come from the store and are Zod-parsed after each patch (`run-manager.ts:2731`). Child outcomes come from the store (`:3245–3274`). B19's working thread adds only `toJson` values (`common.ts:58,70`).

## S5, no literal publication: sound

- **Nothing public is lost.** Every newly projected JSONata site publishes fixed `INTERNAL_ERROR` text today (`run-manager.ts:2645–2660`; `subloop.ts:321–324`; `inference.ts:789–792`). A search for `$error(` finds one use at such a site, `awaited-children.test.ts:1018`, which asserts only resumability.
- **It matches precedent.** B20, poll items and webhook keys already discard the evaluator's message (`primitive-evaluator.ts:279–285`; `poll-items.ts:77–81`; `trigger-service.ts:474–476`).
- **One inconsistency grows.** Mutate and Exit still publish the author's text (`mutation-failures.test.ts:85–87`; `exit.ts:18`). The same operation in an inference transform will not. The ADR should say so.

## Guarded-literal alternative: I agree with declining it

- **The array caveat is real.** `jsonata.js:5651` reads `input.sequence` (`:7532–7534`) before the AST is evaluated at `:5691`, inside the same async call. Its throw cannot be separated by phase. It needs an accessor on an array input, which JSON-derived data cannot carry.
- **It is sound only under the same data-only restriction** the fixed copy already relies on.
- **It buys little.** Only a bare root `$error("literal")` qualifies, an expression that always fails. The conditional and grouped forms (C06, C08–C10) stay fixed copy.
- **It costs a lot.** It needs raw-code capture at `expression.ts:150–155`, an AST-shape contract pinned to 2.2.2, an alphabet that admits a space-only label, and an own-`error` exclusion that also rejects the real built-in (S07).

## R1–R6

- **R1: resolved.** The plan no longer touches `mapHarnessFailure` or the fold. I re-traced three table rows and they equal current values:
  - `contextWindow`/`fits`: `inference.ts:432–443`.

- **S1, S2, S6:** carried unchanged from revision 02. I re-read the B17 path and the workspace port (`workspace.ts:24–27`) and found nothing new.

  - Decision for root: confirm the removal and update that doc row, or keep one correlated private record.

- **Legacy compatibility:** existing `expression.test.ts` passes unmodified, including the overlap and deadline tests (`:42–125`).
- **A1:** `$eval` of a non-compiling string and of an unsafe-regex string at an eligible site gives the generic direction.

- **Unchanged contracts:** P01, P02, B20 and B25 outputs are compared before and after (`mutation-failures.test.ts:79–108`; `flow.test.ts:124–132`).

title: Historical Fable01 REVISE PLAN
body:
# REVISE PLAN — independent critique of the #486 architecture packet

The core design holds against source at `02351e2`, but six parts of the frozen text need narrow amendments before selection. This is a critique only: I ran no commands or tests, and the issue stays `needs-plan-approval`.

## What holds (checked in source)

- **Anchors:** all 26 anchors in `boundaries.md` match this head. A sweep of engine and infrastructure evaluator call sites found none outside B01–B26, P01–P02.
- **Source-local catch is sound:** the evaluators are pure, with no port callback inside. Caller bindings are only `thread`/`index` (`handlers/common.ts:121,136`; `domain/src/mutations.ts:119`; `run-manager.ts:1700–1702`).
- **Separate safe-facts field is needed:** the API serialises `DomainError.details` (`apps/api/src/plugins/errors.ts:192–194`).
- **Guard-first ordering:** strictly reduces effects on blocked visits.
- **Script consent:** untouched (`script-dispatch.ts:60–64,67–94`).
- **No port builds a `RunFailureError`:** zero references in `packages/infrastructure/src`, `packages/adapter-codex/src` and `apps/**/src`.

## Required amendments

### R1. The harness-callback rule rewrites harness policy (README inference bullet 6; verification item 3)

- **Source:**
  - A throw from `start`/`resume` with no handle is classified `definitely-not-submitted` unless the adapter says otherwise (`inference.ts:709–712,797–806`).
  - The maintained matrix asserts this and expects the exact saved prompt on Resume (`testing/inference-failures.ts:131–136`; `inference-evidence-matrix.test.ts:108–117`).
  - Unknown adapter errors legitimately publish their message through the generic fallback (`inference-failure.ts:157–162`; `edge-cases.test.ts:677–689`; `claude.test.ts:398–410`).
  - That same fallback carries the #427 refusal text (`apps/api/src/provider-refusal.test.ts:80–82`).
  - Resumability there is harness-specific (`inference-failure.ts:160`).
- **Fact for root:** same-class harness exceptions are not private today. They publish as `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` with the raw message and `details.adapterCode` set to the domain code. They never receive T/E/M.
- **Reachable case:** a `DomainError` thrown synchronously by `resume` on a repair turn.
  - Today it is not-submitted, and Codex Resume resends the exact repair prompt.
  - Under "retain delivery-uncertain" it becomes a continuation prompt, or non-resumable for an authored turn with no session.
  - "Safe internal copy" also swaps the code to `INTERNAL_ERROR`, bypassing the Claude `retriable` rule and the `HARNESS_DELIVERY_UNCERTAIN` conversion (`inference.ts:823–829,871–874`).
  - Name/code matching is unsound: the repo has an unrelated `TemplateError` with its own codes (`apps/api/src/templates/errors.ts:1–8`).
- **Amendment:**
  - Delete the "insufficient evidence of non-submission / retain delivery-uncertain" sentence and "project safe internal copy".
  - The only harness-side change #486 needs is lifting the two pure renders out of the `contextWindow`/`fits` catch (`inference.ts:432–443`).
  - If root wants true evaluator instances private, limit it to `instanceof DomainError` at the existing observation sites. Substitute only the evidence text (generic code, fixed message, private log) before the unchanged fold, so rank, submission, code conversion and resumability equal a code-less `Error` today.
  - Name/code lookalikes stay ordinary unknown adapter errors.
  - Replace "source and change scope determine exact expected code" with a per-site table of expected code, submission and resumable equal to current values.

### R2. "Restrict recovery" on resolver failure strands a missing-session visit (README inference bullet 1)

- **Source:**
  - `missingFailure` needs the resolved model and effort (`inference.ts:298–302,320–345`).
  - Restorable resolver failures are resumable (`run-manager.ts:2444–2492`).
  - Start fresh session requires the current failure to be `HARNESS_SESSION_MISSING` carrying `missingSession` (`run-manager.ts:1540–1559`; `run-recovery.ts:90–122`).
- **Reachable case:** the process stops after `harness.submission: session-missing` is logged but before `run.failed`. On restart the catalogue temporarily lacks the model.
  - Today: resumable `EVALUATION_UNAVAILABLE`; the next Resume reaches the missing-session failure and its explicit action.
  - Plan: non-resumable with no `missingSession`, so Replay only.
- **Amendment:**
  - Keep the resolver's own code and resumability; attach prior provenance as information only. Guard-first makes that safe.
  - State that the unusable-uncertain guard runs before the resolver, since it needs no model.

### R3. File-return changes exceed the render failure (README subloops bullet 3)

- **Source:** one channel `try` covers resolve, write and receipt append; its catch records `describeError(error).slice(0, 4000)` (`run-manager.ts:3004–3034`). `adversarial.test.ts:379–417` asserts that raw text for `file` and `log`.
- **Reachable case:**
  - "Fixed public delivery copy" for unexpected write failures breaks that contract for `file` only.
  - "Receipt persistence outside any provenance catch" can be read as moving the `return.delivered` append out of the channel catch. A receipt-append failure after a successful write would then fail finalisation and write the file again on reconciliation.
- **Amendment:** add exactly one branch. A local render failure or empty path appends one bounded `return.failed` and skips resolve and write. Leave the existing try/catch, its text and the append position unchanged.

### R4. After-result failures need explicit copy and scope (README inference bullet 5; B18/B19)

- **Source:** any typed failure in the main catch gets `recoveryFailure(pending).message` appended when the turn is `delivery-uncertain` without a usable session (`inference.ts:831–837`; `inference-turn.ts:173–182`).
- **Reachable case:** a harness that never reports a session ID (`edge-cases.test.ts:691–699`) completes, then an output transform fails. The message would end "Prompt delivery is uncertain and no usable session was established…", contradicting the received result.
- **Amendment:**
  - For B18/B19, skip that suffix and use the fixed after-result sentence.
  - Add a fixed `details.phase: "after-result"`.
  - Keep the `delivery-uncertain` enum and leave `accepted` untouched; that part is conservative and invents nothing.
  - Scope the "result received" fact to B18/B19 publication. Applying it to every post-result failure (artifact write, schema mismatch) is a separate harness-policy decision.

### R5. Reserve the child-link keys (B11–B13)

- **Source:** top-level `details.childRunId` drives `PARENT_RECOVERY_REQUIRED` for that child (`run-recovery.ts:61–83`), the inspector's "failed child run" link (`apps/web/src/runs/RunInspectorPage.tsx:57–70`) and wrapper recognition (`failure-publication.ts:48–56`).
- **Reachable case:** an implementer records the mapped child as an "observed effect fact". The succeeded child is then shown as failed and its own Replay is refused.
- **Amendment:** state that new authored details never use `childRunId`, `childNodeId` or `childDetails` at top level. The same-append `child_run.finished` already links the child.

### R6. Name the mapper split and close verification gaps

- **Mapper split:**
  - B14/B19 may share only the hook plumbing (`mutations.ts:45–49,169–171`; `common.ts:266–311`).
  - They must not share Mutate's cause text (`mutate.ts:22–27`), which publishes library messages that tests pin (`mutation-failures.test.ts:87–99`).
  - "Reuse the existing mapper" as written invites raw evaluator text from inference transforms.
- **Missed test:** `awaited-children.test.ts:997–1044` uses `$error("broken")` in `custom.patch`, asserts `resumable` true and resumes to prove completion reuse. It needs the same treatment as `child-creation.test.ts:177–190`.
- **Effect counters (item 4):**
  - Require real sinks through real adapters: a script appending to a counter file, a loopback HTTP log, real filesystem and SQLite.
  - Label harness, structured-completion and classifier counts as scripted-port evidence, not native provider proof.
- **Marker-absence assertions:** exclude P01/P02/B25, and exclude wrappers of pre-change child rows, which copy typed text verbatim (`failure-publication.ts:124–131`).

## Recommended simplifications (optional)

- **S1. Drop `details.childInference` and the recognizer extension.** The existing link reaches the child's authoritative `failure.inference`. If kept: a strict pick of the direct child's own provenance, omitted when absent. Legacy sanitising survives only if `isChildWrapper` accepts exactly that key.
- **S2. Make B17 engine-owned.** The template is a canonical system constant (`inference-context.ts:13–17,42`) that already rendered once. Publish a failure there as a safe internal error rather than a new authored label the author cannot fix.
- **S3. Drop the `intentUnconfirmed`/`retry` re-emission.** The `visitTurn` fold over the earlier `run.failed` already retains the payload across a second preparation failure (`inference-turn.ts:46–66`). Add a regression test instead.
- **S4. Keep only the concrete-evaluator helper form.** A promise-accepting helper cannot stop a port promise being passed. Route `services.render` through the same helper.
- **S5. Tighten the static literal.**
  - Specify ASCII `[A-Za-z0-9 _-]`, non-empty, with an explicit maximum well under 1,000, so the cap (`failure-publication.ts:28–31`) never cuts a label.
  - Add a contract test pinned to jsonata 2.2.2 for the root AST shape and `D3137`.
  - Document that `cond ? x : $error("label")` and `$assert` get fixed copy.
  - Record that the decision contract keeps the same literal private (`flow.test.ts:124–132`).
  - For B08/B12, publish the slug variable name (`contracts/src/nodes.ts:536–539,575–579`) instead of an ordinal.
  - Header ordinals follow JS key order, not strictly declaration order.
- **S6. Workspace tidy-up.** Keep `.trim()` identical and update the comment at `sqlite/workspace-references.ts:55–58`, since the sweep mirrors it. `run-manager.test.ts:38` also overrides `resolve`.

## Root's questions

- **Prior-intent guard and preparation:** preserves prompts, uncertainty and consent, except for R1 (exact retry becomes continuation or refusal) and R2 (fresh-session consent lost).
- **After-result markers:** conservative; no acceptance is invented. Needs R4 for copy and scope.
- **Workspace port:** a clean change with no dual path, provided `view` is removed and the port type excludes `template`. All implementers and callers were found. The journal is unaffected: the SQL triggers read the definition JSON (`drizzle/0023_run_resource_ownership.sql:76–100`).
- **Static literal allowlist:** implementable, since `ast()` is already used (`expression.ts:63,222–224`). `run` must capture the thrown code it currently discards (`expression.ts:150–155`). Sound for root-only, but narrow in usefulness.
- **Nested child shape:** safe and bounded if strict; S1 is simpler.
- **QA:** row/event/REST/MCP/DOM parity is adequate. Counter-effects need the tiering in R6.

## Rejected alternatives

- **Executor-wide `DomainError` catch:** global shape dispatch already misattributes; a workspace error with a `DECIDER_*` code gets decider copy (`run-manager.test.ts:32–66`).
- **A new `PromptSubmission` value for "result received":** contract ripple; the enum plus `details.phase` suffices.
- **Aligning Mutate/Exit to safe causes now:** root's constraint. They remain bounded raw text and can echo runtime values; that is a follow-up issue.
- **Matching `$error` literals anywhere in the AST:** needs an exhaustive walk and leaks value equality.
- **Resumable continuation after B18/B19:** would re-invoke the provider.
- **Resumable expression time-limit failures:** inconsistent with P01/P02/B20. The residual is that a load-induced timeout after an effect forces Replay.

## Evidence limits

- Source reading only; nothing was executed.
- `node_modules` is absent in the worktree, so the jsonata 2.2.2 AST and `D3137`, and the liquidjs 10.30.0 error classes and token position, are unverified against installed bytes.
- Not read: the live issue and admission links, `inventory.json`, and ADRs 0044/0045/0061.
- Only the tests cited were read.
- I did not establish how an out-of-process built API obtains a scripted harness; the in-repo API tests inject `FakeHarness` in process.
